summary: Group Psagot, which owns the once-largest Israeli investment house Psagot, has lost about 80% of its value since Rani Zim bought it for NIS 405 million in August 2021, and now has a market cap of NIS 97 million. Sources blame rising interest rates, the judicial overhaul and the October 7 war, while Zim's inexperience in finance is also cited. The group is seeking to raise NIS 220 million in secured debt, Zim is looking for a buyer, and he is stepping down as chairperson.
one_line: Rani Zim's Psagot investment house has lost about 80% of its value since his 2021 purchase, prompting debt raising, a sale search and his exit as chairperson.
key_facts: Rani Zim bought Psagot Investment House from Altshuler Shaham for NIS 405 million in late August 2021.
Group Psagot (TASE: GPST) now has a market cap of NIS 97 million, after a 75% share price decline in the past year and 80% since the acquisition.
To finance the acquisition, Zim took a NIS 255 million loan from Mizrahi Tefahot Bank and offloaded it onto the acquired investment house; NIS 120 million is still outstanding.
Group Psagot is seeking to raise NIS 220 million in debt secured by its shares in Psagot Investment House, to repay Mizrahi Tefahot and replace NIS 120 million in bonds due within eighteen months.
The existing series C bonds trade at junk yields of around 16%; the group expects yields to fall to single digits after the secured deal.
Zim has invested nearly NIS 130 million of his own capital; his 62% stake in Group Psagot (formerly Value Capital) is worth just NIS 64 million.
Psagot sold one third of its mutual funds business and all of its portfolio management business to Kessem of The Phoenix Holdings group for NIS 200 million.
The mutual funds sale will give Psagot a NIS 90 million gain in Q4, equal to the company's entire market cap.
Psagot's mutual funds took in NIS 1.4 billion in October and NIS 7 billion in the year to end of October, with NIS 43 billion under management, mostly in low-fee money market funds.
Psagot posted a loss of NIS 27 million in the first half of 2023, largely due to its non-bank credit business.
About six weeks earlier, Psagot sold control of AppliCheck to founder Meny Guy and now holds 20% of it.
Zim sought a valuation of around NIS 400 million when he put Psagot up for sale; CEO Yaniv Bender, who holds 7.4%, was mentioned as a possible participant in a buyout.
Rani Zim is stepping down as chairperson of Group Psagot, to be replaced by Daniel Leventhal.
